_internal: `subsistence_from_climate` names the floor per person sim/world/climate_needs.py calculates for each tile from its climate. TRANSITIONAL: surplus_budget_share is a labelled heuristic weight per need (normalised over the needs that have a priced good). A good's effectiveness is per unit of its own production unit, in the need's unit. Mods add needs (ids namespaced by mod id) and add or extend goods; a production entry may also carry `satisfies` and `supply_per_year` for its dominant output. `supply_per_year` states a limited supply with no deposit model behind it, and floors the price at what that supply clears.

food.effectiveness_basis: food energy per kg relative to wheat grain

shelter.unit: cubic metres of wall or frame
shelter.effectiveness_basis: volume of structure one unit builds

clothing.effectiveness_basis: cover and warmth per kg relative to plain woven cloth

implements_and_arms.effectiveness_basis: working hardness and edge holding per kg relative to bronze

health.effectiveness_basis: relative therapeutic or hygienic effect per kg

ornament.unit: kg of bright durable metal equivalent
ornament.satiation_basis: TRANSITIONAL heuristic: ornament metal is durable, so yearly purchase is wear and loss of the stock held, not the budget share; about 25 g held per head and about 2 per cent worn or lost a year. Validation bound used by tests: at most a few grams per head per year. A held-stock model would replace it.
ornament.effectiveness_basis: display value per kg of worked metal; a cultural quantity, equal across the bright metals

seasoning.satiation_basis: TRANSITIONAL heuristic: spices are bought for taste and to dress plain food, and a household's yearly use is grams, not a budget share; a couple of grams per head a year is an order of magnitude, not a measured figure. A model of taste, and of how far an elite's use exceeds the common people's, would replace it.
seasoning.effectiveness_basis: flavouring strength per kg relative to black pepper; taken equal across the spices until a source gives them separately
